name: ANSI/IEEE protective equipotential bonding symbol
summary: IEEE-oriented protective equipotential bond, connecting exposed metal parts together for safety.
description: The protective equipotential bond connects exposed and extraneous conductive parts so that dangerous touch voltages cannot develop between them during a fault. The publisher's IEEE miscellaneous preview lists a protective equipotential bond form, which is the US-practice counterpart of the existing IEC page.

This illustration is an independent explanation and not the IEEE graphic. The bond symbol does not state conductor size or the parts bonded; those belong in bonding schedules. In US terminology this aligns with equipment bonding, which is distinct from the main bonding jumper at the service.
readingNotes: Identify the parts bonded at each symbol.
Distinguish equipment bonding from the service bonding jumper.
drawingChecklist: Keep protective and functional bonds distinct.
distinction: A protective bond is for safety; a functional bond is for equipment operation or noise control.
